title: Infosys Q1 Results: All Eyes on FY27 Guidance as IT Giant Reports Thursday
excerpt: Analysts expect double-digit revenue growth driven by acquisitions, but remain divided on whether Infosys will trim its full-year outlook amid global demand uncertainty.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Infosys expects Q1 FY27 revenue between ₹48,086 crore and ₹48,659 crore, a 13.7–14.9% YoY increase.
  • Brokerages are divided on FY27 revenue growth guidance, estimating 1.5–3% to 2–4%.
  • Operating margins are projected at 21.2–21.4%, supported by cost optimization and no wage hikes.
  • Financial services sector is expected to lead growth, while telecom and manufacturing face challenges.

Infosys, India's second-largest IT services company, will announce its June quarter earnings on Thursday, July 23, after market hours — and the numbers will be parsed as much for what they reveal about global technology spending as for the company's own trajectory.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Oj6oupZVJB4

Revenue Growth Powered by Acquisitions

Brokerage estimates peg revenue in a tight band of ₹48,086 crore to ₹48,659 crore, implying sequential constant currency growth of roughly 2–2.2%. On a year-on-year basis, reported revenue is expected to surge 13.7–14.9%, a figure significantly bolstered by contributions from the Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus acquisitions completed earlier this fiscal year.

Net profit is forecast at ₹8,049 crore to ₹8,173 crore — down 3.9–5.3% sequentially owing to normal quarterly seasonality, but still representing a healthy 16–18.1% jump from the year-ago period.

"Infosys may lead large-cap growth, supported by a two-month contribution from Optimum and Stratus."

— Motilal Oswal Financial Services

The Guidance Question

The headline earnings will matter, but the bigger conversation will centre on whether Infosys revises its FY27 revenue growth guidance, currently set at 1.5–3.5% in constant currency terms.

Brokerages are notably divided. Motilal Oswal expects the company to trim the upper end to 1.5–3%, citing a relatively weaker organic Q1. BNP Paribas, meanwhile, sees a revision to 2–4% once the Optimum Healthcare IT acquisition is factored in. Elara Securities has flagged a higher probability that the upper end comes down, reflecting sluggish discretionary spending.

Equirus Securities offers a more optimistic take, projecting guidance of 2.8–4.3% in constant currency dollar revenue growth, excluding the pending Vertex acquisition.

Margins Expected to Hold Steady

Operating margins are projected in the range of 21.2–21.4%, with some estimates stretching as high as 23.3%. Several tailwinds are at play: the absence of wage hikes during the quarter, a reversal of visa-related costs from Q4, ongoing savings under the company's Project Maximus efficiency programme, and favourable currency movements.

Partially offsetting these gains are acquisition-related amortisation costs, continued investments in artificial intelligence capabilities and the early-stage ramp-up of large deals.

Sector Performance: BFSI Leads, Telecom Lags

Among business verticals, financial services is expected to remain the strongest performer, underpinned by improving client spending in the United States. Energy, utilities and resources should also contribute positively.

The weak spots are familiar: telecom and manufacturing continue to face headwinds from client-specific challenges, including the ongoing ramp-down of the Daimler contract that has weighed on the manufacturing vertical for several quarters.

What to Watch Beyond the Numbers

The management commentary may prove more significant than the headline figures. Investors will focus on updates to the large deal pipeline — which delivered $14.9 billion in total contract value across FY26 — as well as the demand outlook across key geographies and progress on AI-led transformation deals.

The integration of Optimum Healthcare IT and Stratus will also face scrutiny, as will any commentary on discretionary technology spending in the second half of FY27. With the global IT services sector still navigating uncertainty around enterprise budgets, Infosys's outlook on deal momentum and AI adoption will be closely watched across the industry.

For the Indian diaspora's substantial tech workforce — Infosys alone employs over 300,000 people — these results carry implications beyond the balance sheet. Hiring plans, including the company's target of onboarding at least 20,000 freshers in FY27, and any signals about workforce shifts driven by AI adoption will shape career trajectories on both sides of the globe.
